summary: Radar for 2026-10-24, GLP-1 focus only. Three items are fresh enough for Lane C, and the best is a retatrutide double. (1) The NEJM published the Phase 3 TRIUMPH-1-OSA and TRIUMPH-2-OSA sleep apnea trials on Oct 20. In adults without diabetes, the apnea-hypopnea index fell by 34.3 events per hour on 9 mg and 31.7 on 12 mg, versus 9.9 on placebo, at 80 weeks. Coverage was still arriving on Oct 23 (Physicians Weekly, MedPage). (2) The Phase 2b TRANSCEND-CKD trial was presented at ASN Kidney Week on Oct 22: albuminuria down 49.2% versus placebo at 24 weeks, with no change in measured GFR. Retatrutide-named content is our best Shorts lane (median 120). We missed the long-form on the last retatrutide result, so one of these two should get a same-day long-form with a 20:00 funnel Short. (3) ACOG published its first Practice Advisory on GLP-1 medicines in pregnancy and breastfeeding (Healio, Oct 23; Independent and WSJ followed). It's high-search, reassurance-style and fits Instagram, and few creators have covered it yet. The gray-market lane has a citable new hook. A JAMA Network Open study from the University of Pennsylvania analysed about 150,000 Reddit posts from about 40,000 users: increased appetite was the most common complaint about products sold as retatrutide. CBS also had lab tests of 'Reta' bought online done. Lilly's Q3 results on Oct 29 are a dated catalyst. The compounded tirzepatide recall is now peaking in mainstream news, so we use our once-a-week recall slot only. Lane A evergreens refreshed with new hooks: side effects and nausea (Conversation Oct 22, a nausea-measurement review in Diabetes Obes Metab Oct 22), the Wegovy pill versus the shot (fast uptake in real-world data, OCTANE switch data), why GLP-1s work better for some people (the Nature genetics study from April, recirculated Oct 23), menopause, alcohol (Heineken memo), Thanksgiving meals, and stopping. Rejected: sourcing 'research-grade' retatrutide, and 'natural Wegovy' food claims.

candidates.angle: Lane C 'New GLP-1 Drug Decoded': what two Phase 3 trials showed for adults with moderate-to-severe sleep apnea and obesity or overweight, one without type 2 diabetes (n=243) and one with it (n=448). Without diabetes, the apnea-hypopnea index fell by 34.3 events per hour on 9 mg and 31.7 on 12 mg, versus 9.9 on placebo, at 80 weeks. Cover what that means for night-time breathing, what it can't say yet (retatrutide isn't approved, there's no CPAP-replacement claim, and these are trial populations only), and the common side effects (stomach symptoms). Tirzepatide is already approved for sleep apnea; mention it only as context, with no 'beat' framing. 20:00 funnel Short the next day.

candidates.topic: Can you take Ozempic or Mounjaro while pregnant or breastfeeding? ACOG's first Practice Advisory on GLP-1 medicines in pregnancy and lactation (Oct 2026)
candidates.angle: Lane A plus a fresh hook: 'Semaglutide and Pregnancy: What OB-GYNs Now Advise'. ACOG says to counsel patients on the lack of safety data, consider stopping 1–2 months before trying to conceive, discuss reliable contraception (weight loss can raise fertility), and advise against use during pregnancy. Early observational data show no major birth-defect signal after inadvertent first-trimester exposure, but the data are limited. Breastfeeding: shared decision-making with infant-weight monitoring, and ACOG advises against use when the baby is preterm or a newborn. Calm, reassuring tone. No timing instructions beyond quoting ACOG, and 'plan this with your prescriber and OB-GYN'.
